owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to the contract's branch.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.
Never bypass guards: no --no-verify, no bypass env vars, no skip flags.
Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to the contract's branch as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.

tasks.title: Decision record
requirements: Give the workspace a persistent interaction area for the lead agent.
Project brief / scope: objectives, boundaries, assumptions, exclusions, success criteria, stakeholders and approved changes.
Programme roadmap: high-level phases, milestones, dependencies, target dates where known, stage gates and delivery outlook.
Project / delivery plan: the integrated plan showing how scope, schedule, work packages, dependencies, risks, quality and delivery fit together.
Development plan: engineering workstreams, technical sequencing, environments, integration strategy, release stages and technical acceptance criteria.

Work breakdown structure: hierarchical deliverables, work packages, tasks, dependencies, acceptance criteria and status. Users should be able to move from a roadmap milestone to its constituent work packages and tasks and back. Internal task ownership and agent allocation remain Memev-managed.
System architecture: the whole-system design, major components, interfaces, trust boundaries and external dependencies.
Subsystem architecture: drill-down views for individual components, their internal structure, contracts and relationships.
Risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies: a PMO-style RAID view with impact, mitigation and status, linked to affected work.
Canvas / artefacts: generated and user-provided documents, specifications, reports, diagrams, flowcharts, research, code and application previews, with suitable viewers and previews.

Activity / project progress: human-readable updates on completed work, work in progress, milestones, outputs and meaningful changes. Do not make the ordinary customer interface a live agent-routing console or require the user to interpret engine activity.
Blockers / decisions: a dedicated, prominent queue of unresolved issues that genuinely require user input, approval or a decision.
Keep the lead-agent interaction area available across these views, with enough context to understand which project, plan, subsystem, task or artefact the user is discussing.

Make pause, resume, cancel, re-plan, approval and deliverable-acceptance semantics explicit and truthful. A user instruction that changes scope must go through the scope-change process, not silently mutate the approved plan.

If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
